grades.quote: The functions sys_link and sys_unlink edit directories, creating or removing references to inodes.
grades.reason: Describes xv6 sys_link/sys_unlink and the inode link count (nlink), which is background for why a name removal doesn't necessarily destroy the file. It never explains that an open file or remaining reference keeps the file readable after unlink.
Index page listing terms, including 'unlink, 94'. It has no explanation of why a file remains readable after unlink.

grades.quote: Figure 8.16: A file can have two different names, each in its own directory. In this example, the two pathnames `/alpha/beta` and `/gamma/delta` both lead to the same file.
grades.reason: Covers hard links and symbolic links. It shows a file can have multiple names pointing to the same file, so removing one name doesn't remove the file. It also discusses unlink on a symlink target. It doesn't directly explain the open-file-descriptor case or the deferred deletion behind the query.
Contains only a page header and no content related to unlink or reading files afterward.
